content: The translated passage adds two examples: a Maghribi scholar who predicted a great earthquake in 702/1302-3 from Q 99:1 (reported in Ibn Khallikān), and Saʿd al-Dīn Ḥamuvayī's derivation of the states' fortunes from the two Ms of the name Muḥammad, which in his K. al-Maḥbūb mark Samarkand and Damascus. Ibn Turka declines to enter further into such cryptic treatments for fear of boring the reader.
